claim: TAE's dedicated CFP subpage resolves the fields missing from the main page: full papers up to 8 pages excluding references/appendices, appendices allowed with no page limit (reviewers not required to read them), NeurIPS 2026 LaTeX template with the \usepackage[dblblindworkshop]{neurips_2026} option (and [dblblindworkshop, final] for camera-ready), plus a required \workshoptitle{} field.
stance_target: Page limit and format requirements of TAE
quoted_support: Full papers: up to 8 pages, excluding references and appendices. Appendices: allowed, with no page limit, but reviewers are not required to read appendices.

claim: TAE review is explicitly double-blind and the workshop is explicitly non-archival, with all accepted papers presented in an in-person poster session.
stance_target: Anonymity and archival status of TAE
quoted_support: All submissions must be submitted as a single PDF through OpenReview. The review process is double-blind, so please ensure that all papers are appropriately anonymized. All accepted papers will be presented in an in-person poster session. Accepted papers are to be considered non-archival.

claim: TAE's topics of interest include 'uncertainty and robustness' -- explicitly naming stability of evaluation conclusions 'under sampling variation, calibration error, random seeds, data splits, prompts, metrics, evaluator choices' -- closely matching the target paper's Q3 methodology concerns about seed count and sampling variance.
stance_target: Topical fit of TAE for the target paper's methodology-critique framing
quoted_support: Uncertainty and robustness: How stable are evaluation conclusions under sampling variation, calibration error, random seeds, data splits, prompts, metrics, evaluator choices, noisy or delayed feedback, tail risk, and worst-case behavior?

claim: TAE's stated core gap is methodological: many evaluation claims do not state what is measured, how it becomes a protocol, or what inference the protocol supports -- the workshop studies evaluation protocols themselves, not only the models being evaluated, but has no explicit statement welcoming negative results specifically.
stance_target: Whether TAE has an explicit stated position on negative results
quoted_support: The core gap is methodological. Many evaluation claims do not state what is measured, how it becomes a protocol, or what inference the protocol supports. We invite submissions that study evaluation protocols themselves, not only the models being evaluated.
